tickets.title: Quality of life and e-bike storage on 11th Street
tickets.summary: Public speakers and the District Manager describe more than 100 electric delivery bikes stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and 1st Avenue, blocking sidewalks, driving out businesses, and raising fire concerns. The District Manager says the precinct plans an enforcement action on October 7 that could confiscate bikes, and speakers asked for advance notice, translated warnings, and an alternative to enforcement. Action: Ask the precinct and district office to give delivery workers multilingual notice before enforcement and to help find a legal parking or corral site for the bikes.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Niles Robinson (borough president's office liaison); Susan (District Manager); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Drug use and homelessness in Seward Park and nearby parks have increased, and the Lower East Side Ecology Center reported problems near a bathroom used by drug users. The precinct has a task force with police stationed at the park, and the park also has dark spots that let drug use go unseen. Action: Ask the precinct and Parks Department to report on enforcement and outreach results and to fix or report out-of-service park lights, and consider expanding mobile crisis response.

tickets.title: Closing Third Avenue L station study and pilot
tickets.summary: A public speaker who rides the L train argues that the Third Avenue station has very few boardings and that closing it would save riders time based on his simulation of MTA trip data. He notes the station is not a transfer point and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the district office to request a pilot closure of the Third Avenue stop with the MTA.

tickets.title: Proposed denial of 11 Allen Street liquor license
tickets.summary: The board voted to recommend denial of a full liquor license for 11 Allen Street, a new location for an operator tied to the problematic Time Cafe at Forsyth and Canal. Speakers cited a saturated area near Dime Square, crowds outside Time Cafe, and the lack of a stipulated agreement if the applicant goes straight to the SLA. Action: Ask board members and community members to attend the State Liquor Authority hearing to support the denial, and have staff gather 311 complaint data for the record.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community requirements
tickets.summary: The Land Use and Economic Development subcommittee met with EDC on the Essex Market RFP, which was due to go out at the end of the month. EDC could not say whether the board's two resolutions on keeping the market community-focused were included. Action: Ask EDC to postpone issuing the RFP and to confirm how the board's resolutions are reflected, with a follow-up meeting this week.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee (board members)
tickets.summary: A resolution proposes a mobile-first voting option for Community Education Council elections because turnout has been around 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers said outreach must explain eligibility and reassure immigrant families that their information will not be used against them. Action: Send the resolution to the New York City Department of Education urging a mobile voting pilot and expanded multilingual parent outreach about CEC voting.

tickets.title: Pilot public restrooms in the district
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, one near Delancey and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. Concerns were raised about access, who can use them, and emergency calls, and the board is preparing a resolution on the pilot. Action: Vote on a resolution next month setting out access rules and what the board wants during the pilot, and have staff work with DOT and the vendor on it.

tickets.title: Attendance and removal bylaws revision
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would handle repeated absences through a letter and an executive committee meeting before any removal, drop attendance from the general removal process, and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. A speaker noted the executive committee role was unclear, and the chair said the change is not punitive. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaw changes at the October full board meeting, with notice sent at least 28 days in advance.
